extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT work)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and formalize the definitions, structural requirements, and symmetry/indeterminacy properties for the objects introduced (base-NF-bridges, base-Θ-bridges, D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) and the requirements for the "desired geometry" used in this part of IUT theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for the "desired geometry"
rubrics_metrics.description: The desired geometry to be used must satisfy three explicit requirements listed in the text: (a) local independence of global structures, (b) globalizability in a fashion that is independent of local structures, (c) the property of being based on 'étale-like structures'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that (a) and (b) at first glance almost contradict one another and that their simultaneous realization is highly nontrivial (e.g., for function fields of dimension one one might be forced to descend to the base field). The mono-anabelian geometry developed in [AbsTopIII] is cited as satisfying all these requirements. The geometry must admit localization operations to various local geometries while giving rise to the global arithmetic (ring structure and absolute Galois groups) in a way independent of local geometries; being 'étale-like' is necessary to obtain canonical splittings as in the étale-picture (see Corollary 3.9(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a base-NF-bridge (D-NF-bridge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-NF-bridge (D-NF-bridge) relative to the given initial Θ-data is defined to be a poly-morphism †DJ (†φNF)−→ †D(cid:6) where †D(cid:6) is a category equivalent to D(cid:6) and †DJ = {†Dj}j∈J is a capsule of D-prime-strips indexed by a finite index set J, such that there exist isomorphisms D(cid:6) ∼→ †D(cid:6), D(cid:2) ∼→ †DJ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An [iso]morphism of D-NF-bridges (†DJ †φNF−→ †D(cid:6)) → (‡DJ ‡φNF−→ ‡D(cid:6)) is a pair of poly-morphisms †DJ ∼→ ‡DJ (a capsule-full poly-isomorphism) and †D(cid:6) ∼→ ‡D(cid:6) (a poly-morphism that is an Aut(†D(cid:6))- [or Aut(‡D(cid:6))-] orbit), compatible with the respective φNF. There is an evident composition law for morphisms of D-NF-bridges. (The definition is presented as a precise structural requirement for what counts as a D-NF-bridge.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a base-Θ-bridge (D-Θ-bridge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-Θ-bridge (D-Θ-bridge) relative to the given initial Θ-data is a poly-morphism †DJ (†φΘ)−→ †D> where †D> is a D-prime-strip and †DJ = {†Dj}j∈J is a capsule of D-prime-strips indexed by a finite index set J, such that there exist isomorphisms D> ∼→ †D>, D(cid:2) ∼→ †DJ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An [iso]morphism of D-Θ-bridges is defined analogously to the NF case: a pair of poly-morphisms †DJ ∼→ ‡DJ (capsule-full poly-isomorphism) and †D> ∼→ ‡D> (full poly-isomorphism) compatible with the φΘ. Composition of morphisms of D-Θ-bridges is evident. This is a structural/definitional criterion specifying when a poly-morphism qualifies as a D-Θ-bridge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a base-ΘNF-Hodge theater (D-ΘNF-Hodge theater)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-ΘNF-Hodge theater relative to the initial Θ-data is a collection of data †HT D-ΘNF = (†D(cid:6) †φNF←− †DJ †φΘ−→ †D>) where the left arrow is a D-NF-bridge and the right arrow is a D-Θ-bridge, and there exist isomorphisms D(cid:6) ∼→ †D(cid:6), D(cid:2) ∼→ †DJ , D> ∼→ †D>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An [iso]morphism of D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters is a pair of morphisms between the associated D-NF- and D-Θ-bridges inducing the same bijection between index sets of the capsules. There is an evident composition of morphisms. This defines the required structure and compatibility conditions for such theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and torsor properties of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Proposition 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 4.7 asserts structural properties that a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater must produce: (i) the structure at v ∈ Vbad of the D-Θ-bridge determines a bijection †χ: π0(†DJ)=J ∼→ F_l (i.e., labels in F_l for constituent D-prime-strips); (ii) for each j ∈ J, restriction via the j-indexed portions determines an isomorphism of F_l-torsors †φLC_j : LabCusp(†D(cid:6)) ∼→ LabCusp(†D>), with specified equivariance (†φLC_j obtained from †φLC_1 by composing with action by †χ(j) ∈ F_l); (iii) there exists a unique element [†(cid:2)] ∈ LabCusp(†D(cid:6)) giving a canonical bijection †ζ(cid:2): LabCusp(†D(cid:6)) ∼→ J (∼→ F_l via †χ), independent up to composition with multiplication by an element of F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are exact structural constraints/outputs that a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater must furnish: canonical label bijections, F_l-torsor isomorphisms coming from restriction at places, and a distinguished global cusp class whose translations yield the label assignment. The independence statement (up to F_l action) is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism / symmetry properties of bridges and theaters (Proposition 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic formal properties required/ensured for the defined objects: (i) the set of isomorphisms between two D-NF-bridges forms an F_l-torsor; (ii) the set of isomorphisms between two D-Θ-bridges (resp. two D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) has cardinality one (i.e., is unique); (iii) given a D-NF-bridge and a D-Θ-bridge, the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms between their capsules that allow gluing into a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater forms an F_l-torsor; (iv) given a D-NF-bridge, there exists a functorial algorithm to construct, up to an F_l-indeterminacy, a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater whose underlying D-NF-bridge is the given one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items specify the allowed indeterminacies and uniqueness statements that govern constructions and comparisons: when constructions are unique, when they are only defined up to an F_l-torsor, and that an explicit (relatively simple) algorithm exists for building a theater from an NF-bridge up to that torsor indeterminacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetries arising from forgetful functors (Proposition 4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The forgetful/associated functors produce canonical symmetry actions: (i) forgetting to the underlying D-NF-bridge yields a functor whose output admits an F_l-symmetry acting simply transitively on the index set J of the capsule of D-prime-strips; (ii) forgetting to the underlying capsule of D-prime-strips (i.e., forgetting labels) yields an Sl-symmetry (symmetric group on l letters) acting transitively on the index set J, meaning that given the capsule up to isomorphism there are precisely l choices for the element of F_l corresponding to a given index prior to applying the functor; (iii) composing (ii) with mono-analyticization yields an analogous functor to capsules of D(cid:4)-prime-strips with the same symmetry properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functorial symmetries explain how label indeterminacy arises and how forgetting structure enlarges symmetry (F_l vs S_l), thereby describing the exact form of permissible permutations and torsor actions used later to compare objects constructed relative to different labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of G-conjugacy indeterminacies and factorization uniqueness (Remark 4.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When subgroups J ⊆ H ⊆ G are only known up to conjugacy in G, one should consider collections of outer homomorphisms J_out → H_out compatible with structure morphisms to G_out; this records all inclusions J^{g1} → H^{g2} for g1,g2∈G without imposing arbitrary synchronization choices. Two distinct natural conditions are distinguished: (∗⊆) that I be a G-conjugate of J (independent of datum H*), and (∗∼=) that I be a G-conjugate of J such that (H*,I) ≅ (H,J) (which depends on H* and imposes a partial synchronization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the concrete examples, at v∈Vbad a factorization J→H→G is uniquely determined by the composite J→G (i.e., by the chosen G-conjugate of J) without synchronizing indeterminacies; at v∈Varc uniqueness is weaker — only the H-conjugacy class of the image is determined. The guidance is to work with outer homomorphisms and to avoid arbitrary synchronization choices; this distinction is central for later Hodge-Arakelov theoretic evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of evaluation points and evaluation sections (Example 4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v∈Vbad there is a natural bijection |F_l| = F_l/{±1} with cusps of the hyperbolic orbicurve C_v; one defines a special torsion point μ− of order 2 and uses μ−-translates of cusps (relative to the elliptic curve group scheme) as evaluation points of X_v. The values of the theta function Θ at points lying over these evaluation points lie in the μ2l-orbit of {q_j^2_v}_j, and the points of X that lie over these evaluation points are defined over K_v. One obtains evaluation sections Π_v → G_v of the natural surjection Π_v (two-headed arrow) G_v; there is a group-theoretic algorithm for constructing the evaluation sections from isomorphs of the topological group Π_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes how to produce evaluation points/sections group-theoretically and indicates their arithmetic definability (over K_v). It also notes that the induced homomorphisms on π1 are well-defined up to inner automorphism and compatible with outer actions on geometric (tempered) fundamental groups, a fact summarized as 'φΘ_vj(D_vj), πgeo(D_vj) ∼→ πgeo(D>,v)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-labelled output data and symmetry actions to compare arithmetic constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-labelled output data produced by the forgetful functors (Propositions 4.9(i),(ii),(iii)) — i.e., capsules or underlying D-NF-bridges without labels — are crucial for comparing objects (e.g., arithmetic line bundles, log-volumes) constructed relative to different labels. The F_l-symmetry that appears acts transitively on indices and can be used to perform the comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains that to compute global log-volumes one must compare local log-volumes arising at D-prime-strips with different labels; forgetting labels (or considering non-labelled output) and employing the symmetry actions provide the mechanism to compare such quantities while minimizing label indeterminacy. Later constructions (e.g., 'processions') are used to further minimize label ambiguities.
